Entomology.subject: Agricultural Entomology

Entomology.fact: While not true entomologists in the traditional sense, individuals who attain the ACE certification may be called ACEs or Associate Certified Entomologists.

Entomology.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Entomology.question: As such, other credential programs managed by the _____ of America have varying credential requirements
Entomology.fact: As such, other credential programs managed by the Entomological Society of America have varying credential requirements.

Entomology.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Entomology.question: These individuals also have to "agree to ascribe to a code of ethical behavior" (ESA _____)
Entomology.fact: These different programs are called Public Health Entomology (PHE), Certified IPM Technicians (CITs), and Board Certified Entomologists (BCEs) (ESA Certification Corporation). To be qualified in public health entomology (PHE), one must pass an exam on the types of arthropods that can spread diseases and lead to medical complications (ESA Certification Corporation).

Entomology.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Entomology.question: These individuals must also be approved to use pesticides (ESA _____)
Entomology.fact: These individuals also have to "agree to ascribe to a code of ethical behavior" (ESA Certification Corporation). Entomology.fact: Like in Public Health Entomology (PHE), those who want to become Certified IPM Technicians (CITs) also have to "agree to ascribe to a code of ethical behavior" (ESA Certification Corporation). Insect.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Insect.question: In his 1817 Le Règne Animal, _____ grouped all animals into four embranchements ("branches" with different body plans), one of which was the articulated animals, containing arthropods and annelids
Insect.fact: In his 1817 Le Règne Animal, Georges Cuvier grouped all animals into four embranchements ("branches" with different body plans), one of which was the articulated animals, containing arthropods and annelids.

Insect.subject: Agricultural Entomology

Insect.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Insect.question: The oldest known flying insects are from the mid-Carboniferous, around 328–_____ years ago
Insect.fact: The oldest known flying insects are from the mid-Carboniferous, around 328–324 million years ago.

Insect.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Insect.question: Claims that they originated substantially earlier, during the Silurian or Devonian (some _____ years ago) based on molecular clock estimates, are unlikely to be correct, given the fossil record
Insect.fact: Claims that they originated substantially earlier, during the Silurian or Devonian (some 400 million years ago) based on molecular clock estimates, are unlikely to be correct, given the fossil record.

Insect.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Insect.question: Four large-scale radiations of insects have occurred: beetles (from about _____ years ago), flies (from about 250 million years ago), moths and wasps (both from about 150 million years ago)
Insect.fact: Four large-scale radiations of insects have occurred: beetles (from about 300 million years ago), flies (from about 250 million years ago), moths and wasps (both from about 150 million years ago).

Insect.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Insect.question: The extremely successful Hymenoptera (wasps, bees, and ants) appeared some _____ years ago in the Triassic Period, but achieved their wide diversity more recently in the Cenozoic era, which began 66 m
Insect.fact: The extremely successful Hymenoptera (wasps, bees, and ants) appeared some 200 million years ago in the Triassic Period, but achieved their wide diversity more recently in the Cenozoic era, which began 66 million years ago.

Insect.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Insect.question: The abdomen is the largest part of the insect, typically with _____–12 segments, and is less strongly sclerotized than the head or thorax
Insect.fact: The abdomen is the largest part of the insect, typically with 11–12 segments, and is less strongly sclerotized than the head or thorax.

Insect.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Insect.question: Phylogenetic analysis suggests that UV-green-blue trichromacy existed from at least the Devonian Period, some _____ years ago
Insect.fact: Phylogenetic analysis suggests that UV-green-blue trichromacy existed from at least the Devonian Period, some 400 million years ago.

Insect.subject: Agricultural Entomology

Insect.fact: The most familiar group are the fireflies, beetles of the family Lampyridae.

Insect.fact: Some fireflies of the genus Photuris mimic the flashing of female Photinus species to attract males of that species, which are then captured and devoured.

Insect.fact: The colors of emitted light vary from dull blue (Orfelia fultoni, Mycetophilidae) to the familiar greens and the rare reds (Phrixothrix tiemanni, Phengodidae).

Insect.fact: Some moths produce ultrasonic clicks that warn predatory bats of their unpalatability (acoustic aposematism), while some palatable moths have evolved to mimic these calls (acoustic Batesian mimicry).

Insect.subject: Agricultural Entomology

Insect.fact: A small number of species such as Water striders can move on the surface of water; their claws are recessed in a special groove, preventing the claws from piercing the water's surface film. In some groups, such as water beetles, the adults too are aquatic.

Insect.fact: Chemical defense is common among Coleoptera and Lepidoptera, usually being advertised by bright warning colors (aposematism), as in the monarch butterfly.

Insect.question: Some ground beetles of the family _____ actively defend themselves, spraying chemicals from their abdomen with great accuracy, to repel predators
Insect.fact: Some ground beetles of the family Carabidae actively defend themselves, spraying chemicals from their abdomen with great accuracy, to repel predators.

Insect.subject: Agricultural Entomology

Insect.fact: Beekeeping in pottery vessels began about 9,000 years ago in North Africa.

Insect.fact: A larger 2020 meta-study, analyzing data from 166 long-term surveys, suggested that populations of terrestrial insects are indeed decreasing rapidly, by about 9% per decade.

Metamorphosis.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Metamorphosis.question: The _____ was Profound change in body structure during the postembryonic development of an organism.
Metamorphosis.fact: Metamorphosis is a biological process in which an animal undergoes a conspicuous and relatively abrupt change in its body structure as part of its development. Some insects, fish, amphibians, mollusks, crustaceans, cnidarians, echinoderms, and tunicates undergo metamorphosis, often accompanied by a change of nutrition or behavior.

Metamorphosis.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Metamorphosis.question: Phylogenetically, all insects in the _____ undergo a marked change in form, texture and physical appearance from immature stage to adult
Metamorphosis.fact: Phylogenetically, all insects in the Pterygota undergo a marked change in form, texture and physical appearance from immature stage to adult.

Metamorphosis.subject: Agricultural Entomology

Metamorphosis.fact: Leptocephali are common, occurring in all Elopomorpha (tarpon- and eel-like fish).

Metamorphosis.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Metamorphosis.question: Within the genus _____, species have evolved to be pedomorphic several times, and pedomorphosis and complete development can both occur in some species
Metamorphosis.fact: Within the genus Ambystoma, species have evolved to be pedomorphic several times, and pedomorphosis and complete development can both occur in some species.

Metamorphosis.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Metamorphosis.question: More recently diverged caecilians (the _____) do not undergo an ontogenetic niche shift of this sort and are in general fossorial throughout their lives
Metamorphosis.fact: More recently diverged caecilians (the Teresomata) do not undergo an ontogenetic niche shift of this sort and are in general fossorial throughout their lives.

Larva.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Larva.question: The _____ was Juvenile form of distinct animals before metamorphosis.
Larva.fact: A larva (; pl.: larvae ) is a distinct juvenile form many animals undergo before metamorphosis into their next life stage. Animals with indirect development such as insects, some arachnids, amphibians, or cnidarians typically have a larval phase of their life cycle.

Larva.subject: Agricultural Entomology

Pollinator.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Pollinator.question: The _____ was Animal that moves pollen from the male anther of a flower to the female stigma.
Pollinator.fact: A pollinator is an animal that moves pollen from the male anther of a flower to the female stigma of a flower. Insects are the major pollinators of most plants, and insect pollinators include all families of bees and most families of aculeate wasps; ants; many families of flies; many lepidopterans (both butterflies and moths); and many families of beetles.

Pollinator.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Pollinator.question: In _____, researchers showed evidence of pollination occurring underwater, which was previously thought not to happen

Pollinator.subject: Agricultural Entomology

Pollinator.fact: The orchid species Epipactis veratrifolia mimics alarm pheromones of aphids to attract hover flies for pollination.

Pollinator.fact: A 2021 study estimated that without pollinators, fertility would be reduced by 80% in half all wild plant species and one-third of all wild plant species would fail to produce any seeds at all.

Caterpillar.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Caterpillar.question: It was described under _____ vadens
Caterpillar.fact: It was described under Eogeometer vadens.

Caterpillar.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Caterpillar.question: Previously, another fossil dating back approximately 125 million years was found in _____ amber
Caterpillar.fact: Previously, another fossil dating back approximately 125 million years was found in Lebanese amber.

Caterpillar.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Caterpillar.question: Previously, another fossil dating back approximately _____ years was found in Lebanese amber
Caterpillar.fact: Previously, another fossil dating back approximately 125 million years was found in Lebanese amber.

Caterpillar.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Caterpillar.question: Some Arctic species like _____ groenlandica have special basking and aggregation behaviours apart from physiological adaptations to remain in a dormant state
Caterpillar.fact: Some Arctic species like Gynaephora groenlandica have special basking and aggregation behaviours apart from physiological adaptations to remain in a dormant state.

Caterpillar.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Caterpillar.question: A venom which is among the most potent defensive chemicals in any animal is produced by the _____ silk moth genus Lonomia
Caterpillar.fact: A venom which is among the most potent defensive chemicals in any animal is produced by the South American silk moth genus Lonomia.

Caterpillar.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Caterpillar.question: Its venom is an anticoagulant powerful enough to cause a human to hemorrhage to death (_____)
Caterpillar.fact: Its venom is an anticoagulant powerful enough to cause a human to hemorrhage to death (See Lonomiasis).

Caterpillar.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Caterpillar.question: These toxic species, such as the cinnabar moth (Tyria jacobaeae) and monarch (Danaus plexippus) caterpillars, usually advertise themselves with the warning colors of red, yellow and _____, often in bright stripes
Caterpillar.fact: These toxic species, such as the cinnabar moth (Tyria jacobaeae) and monarch (Danaus plexippus) caterpillars, usually advertise themselves with the warning colors of red, yellow and black, often in bright stripes.

Caterpillar.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Caterpillar.question: One species (_____ juglandis) even makes high pitched whistles that can scare away birds
Caterpillar.fact: One species (Amorpha juglandis) even makes high pitched whistles that can scare away birds.

Caterpillar.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Caterpillar.question: A few are parasitic on cicadas or leaf hoppers (_____)
Caterpillar.fact: A few are parasitic on cicadas or leaf hoppers (Epipyropidae).

Caterpillar.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Caterpillar.question: For example, the "cutworms" (of the family _____) hide at the base of plants during the day and only feed at night
Caterpillar.fact: For example, the "cutworms" (of the family Noctuidae) hide at the base of plants during the day and only feed at night.

Caterpillar.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Caterpillar.question: Others, such as spongy moth (Lymantria dispar) larvae, change their activity patterns depending on density and larval stage, with more diurnal feeding in early instars and _____ densities
Caterpillar.fact: Others, such as spongy moth (Lymantria dispar) larvae, change their activity patterns depending on density and larval stage, with more diurnal feeding in early instars and high densities.

Caterpillar.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Caterpillar.question: Lonomia is a frequent cause of envenomation in Brazil, with 354 cases reported between _____ and 2005
Caterpillar.fact: Lonomia is a frequent cause of envenomation in Brazil, with 354 cases reported between 1989 and 2005.

Caterpillar.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Caterpillar.question: Caterpillars of most species eat plant material (often leaves), but not all; some (about _____) eat insects, and some are even cannibalistic
Caterpillar.fact: Caterpillars of most species eat plant material (often leaves), but not all; some (about 1%) eat insects, and some are even cannibalistic.

Caterpillar.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Caterpillar.question: Lethality ranging up to _____ with death caused most often by intracranial hemorrhage
Caterpillar.fact: Lethality ranging up to 20% with death caused most often by intracranial hemorrhage.

Caterpillar.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Caterpillar.question: For example, in _____ mopane worms are eaten by the bushmen, and in China silkworms are considered a delicacy
Caterpillar.fact: For example, in South Africa mopane worms are eaten by the bushmen, and in China silkworms are considered a delicacy.

Caterpillar.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Caterpillar.question: In _____ William Blake referenced this popular image in The Marriage of Heaven and Hell when he attacked priests: "as the caterpillar chooses the fairest leaves to lay her eggs on, so the priest lay h
Caterpillar.fact: In 1790 William Blake referenced this popular image in The Marriage of Heaven and Hell when he attacked priests: "as the caterpillar chooses the fairest leaves to lay her eggs on, so the priest lay his curse on the fairest joys".

Caterpillar.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Caterpillar.question: In _____ Maria Sibylla Merian published the first volume of The Caterpillars' Marvelous Transformation and Strange Floral Food, which contained 50 illustrations and a description of insects, moths, bu
Caterpillar.fact: In 1679 Maria Sibylla Merian published the first volume of The Caterpillars' Marvelous Transformation and Strange Floral Food, which contained 50 illustrations and a description of insects, moths, butterflies and their larvae.

Caterpillar.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Caterpillar.question: Butterflies were regarded as symbol for the human soul since ancient time, and also in the _____ tradition
Caterpillar.fact: Butterflies were regarded as symbol for the human soul since ancient time, and also in the Christian tradition. Goedart thus located his empirical observations on the transformation of caterpillars into butterflies in the Christian tradition.

Chemical communication in insects.fact: In 1965, the entomologist Edward O. Wilson published a paper on chemical communication in the social insects, arguing that their societies were principally organised by "complex systems of chemical signals".

Chemical communication in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical communication in insects.question: In 1965, the entomologist _____ published a paper on chemical communication in the social insects, arguing that their societies were principally organised by "complex systems of chemical signals"
Chemical communication in insects.fact: In 1965, the entomologist Edward O. Wilson published a paper on chemical communication in the social insects, arguing that their societies were principally organised by "complex systems of chemical signals".

Chemical communication in insects.question: By _____, Mahmoud Ali and David Morgan noted that the field had grown too large to review comprehensively
Chemical communication in insects.fact: By 1990, Mahmoud Ali and David Morgan noted that the field had grown too large to review comprehensively.

Chemical communication in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical communication in insects.question: By 1990, _____ and David Morgan noted that the field had grown too large to review comprehensively
Chemical communication in insects.fact: By 1990, Mahmoud Ali and David Morgan noted that the field had grown too large to review comprehensively.

Chemical communication in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical communication in insects.question: They can be grouped by which individuals they act upon: _____ serve communication between insects of the same species
Chemical communication in insects.fact: Types of semiochemicals include pheromones and kairomones. They can be grouped by which individuals they act upon: Pheromones serve communication between insects of the same species.

Chemical communication in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical communication in insects.question: Primers include the queen pheromones essential to maintain the caste structure of social _____ colonies; they tend to be non-volatile and are dispersed by workers across the colony
Chemical communication in insects.fact: Primers include the queen pheromones essential to maintain the caste structure of social Hymenopteran colonies; they tend to be non-volatile and are dispersed by workers across the colony.

Chemical communication in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical communication in insects.question: These include mandibular glands in the head, and _____'s, tergal, and other glands in the abdomen
Chemical communication in insects.fact: These include mandibular glands in the head, and Dufour's, tergal, and other glands in the abdomen.

Chemical defense in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical defense in insects.question: Reflexive bleeding occurs in specific parts of the body; for example, the beetle families _____ (ladybugs) and Meloidae bleed from the knee joints
Chemical defense in insects.fact: Reflexive bleeding occurs in specific parts of the body; for example, the beetle families Coccinellidae (ladybugs) and Meloidae bleed from the knee joints.

Chemical defense in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical defense in insects.question: Pasteels, Grégoire, and _____-Rahier have grouped chemical defenses into three types: compounds that are truly poisonous, those that restrict movement, and those that repel predators
Chemical defense in insects.fact: Pasteels, Grégoire, and Rowell-Rahier have grouped chemical defenses into three types: compounds that are truly poisonous, those that restrict movement, and those that repel predators.

Chemical defense in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical defense in insects.question: True poisons, essentially _____ I compounds, interfere with specific physiological processes or act at certain sites
Chemical defense in insects.fact: The two different classes are not mutually exclusive, and insects may use combinations of the two. True poisons, essentially Class I compounds, interfere with specific physiological processes or act at certain sites.

Chemical defense in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical defense in insects.question: Repellents are similar to those classified under _____ as they irritate the chemical sensitivity of predators
Chemical defense in insects.fact: Repellents are similar to those classified under Class II as they irritate the chemical sensitivity of predators. This last grouping of chemicals has both Class I and Class II properties.

Chemical defense in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical defense in insects.question: This last grouping of chemicals has both _____ I and Class II properties
Chemical defense in insects.fact: True poisons, essentially Class I compounds, interfere with specific physiological processes or act at certain sites. Repellents are similar to those classified under Class II as they irritate the chemical sensitivity of predators.

Chemical defense in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical defense in insects.question: In nasute species of termites (contained within the subfamily _____), the mandibles have receded
Chemical defense in insects.fact: In nasute species of termites (contained within the subfamily Nasutitermitinae), the mandibles have receded.

Chemical defense in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical defense in insects.question: Among termite species in the _____ that are soldierless or where soldiers are rare, mouth secretions are commonly replaced by abdominal dehiscence
Chemical defense in insects.fact: Among termite species in the Apicotermitinae that are soldierless or where soldiers are rare, mouth secretions are commonly replaced by abdominal dehiscence.

Chemical defense in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical defense in insects.question: Within the subfamily _____, the stinger has been lost and instead the poison gland forcibly ejects the fluid of choice, formic acid
Chemical defense in insects.fact: Within the subfamily Formicinae, the stinger has been lost and instead the poison gland forcibly ejects the fluid of choice, formic acid.

Chemical defense in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical defense in insects.question: Some carpenter ants (genus _____) also have mandibular glands that extend throughout their bodies
Chemical defense in insects.fact: Some carpenter ants (genus Camponotus) also have mandibular glands that extend throughout their bodies.

Chemical defense in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical defense in insects.question: The subfamily _____, which also does not possess a stinger, has a different type of defense
Chemical defense in insects.fact: The subfamily Dolichoderinae, which also does not possess a stinger, has a different type of defense.

Chemical defense in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical defense in insects.question: This inhibition leads to neurodegeneration with symptoms similar to those caused by _____'s disease
Chemical defense in insects.fact: This inhibition leads to neurodegeneration with symptoms similar to those caused by Huntington's disease.

Chemical defense in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical defense in insects.question: The larvae of _____ leaf beetles developed a second defensive strategy that is based on the excretion of droplets via pairs of defensive glands at the back of the insects
Chemical defense in insects.fact: The larvae of Chrysomelina leaf beetles developed a second defensive strategy that is based on the excretion of droplets via pairs of defensive glands at the back of the insects.

Chemical defense in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical defense in insects.question: For instance, the red poplar leaf beetle (_____ populi) consumes the leaves of poplar plants, which contain salicin
Chemical defense in insects.fact: For instance, the red poplar leaf beetle (Chrysomela populi) consumes the leaves of poplar plants, which contain salicin.

Chemical defense in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical defense in insects.question: The hemolymph toxins originate from autogenous de novo biosynthesis by the _____ beetle
Chemical defense in insects.fact: The hemolymph toxins originate from autogenous de novo biosynthesis by the Chrysomelina beetle. Essential amino acids, such as valine serve as precursors for the production of the hemolymph toxins of Chrysomelina leaf beetles.

Chemical defense in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical defense in insects.question: Essential amino acids, such as valine serve as precursors for the production of the hemolymph toxins of _____ leaf beetles
Chemical defense in insects.fact: The hemolymph toxins originate from autogenous de novo biosynthesis by the Chrysomelina beetle. Essential amino acids, such as valine serve as precursors for the production of the hemolymph toxins of Chrysomelina leaf beetles.

Chemical defense in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical defense in insects.question: Free 3-NPA and glucosides that derive from 3-NPA and isoxazolin-5-one also occur in many genera of leguminous plants (_____)
Chemical defense in insects.fact: Free 3-NPA and glucosides that derive from 3-NPA and isoxazolin-5-one also occur in many genera of leguminous plants (Fabaceae).

Chemical defense in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical defense in insects.question: The larvae of leaf beetles from the subfamilies of e.g., _____ and Galerucinae often employ fecal shields, masses of feces that they carry on their bodies to repel predators
Chemical defense in insects.fact: The larvae of leaf beetles from the subfamilies of e.g., Criocerinae and Galerucinae often employ fecal shields, masses of feces that they carry on their bodies to repel predators.

Chemical defense in insects.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Chemical defense in insects.question: These wasps possess a gland located in the VI abdominal sternite (van de _____'s gland) that is primarily responsible for making an ant-repellent substance
Chemical defense in insects.fact: These wasps possess a gland in the VI abdominal sternite (van de Vecht's gland) that is primarily responsible for making an ant-repellent substance.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: The _____ was Aquatic animal phylum having cnidocytes.
Cnidaria.fact: Cnidaria ( nih-DAIR-ee-ə, ny-) is a phylum of animals containing over 11,000 species of aquatic invertebrates found both in freshwater and marine environments (predominantly the latter), including jellyfish, hydroids, sea anemones, corals and some of the smallest marine parasites. Many cnidarian species can reproduce both sexually and asexually.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: Several free-swimming species of _____ and Scyphozoa possess balance-sensing statocysts, and some have simple eyes
Cnidaria.fact: Several free-swimming species of Cubozoa and Scyphozoa possess balance-sensing statocysts, and some have simple eyes.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: Staurozoa have recently been recognised as a class in their own right rather than a sub-group of Scyphozoa, and the highly derived parasitic Myxozoa and Polypodiozoa were firmly recognized as cnidaria
Cnidaria.fact: Staurozoa have recently been recognised as a class in their own right rather than a sub-group of Scyphozoa, and the highly derived parasitic Myxozoa and Polypodiozoa were firmly recognized as cnidarians only in 2007.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: Other polyps such as _____ use columns of water-filled cells for support
Cnidaria.fact: Other polyps such as Tubularia use columns of water-filled cells for support.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: In Anthozoa (anemones, corals, etc.) and _____ (jellyfish), the mesoglea also contains some muscle cells
Cnidaria.fact: In Anthozoa (anemones, corals, etc.) and Scyphozoa (jellyfish), the mesoglea also contains some muscle cells.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: Three types of cnidocytes are known: _____ inject venom into prey, and usually have barbs to keep them embedded in the victims
Cnidaria.fact: Three types of cnidocytes are known: Nematocysts inject venom into prey, and usually have barbs to keep them embedded in the victims. Most species have nematocysts.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: Ptychocysts are found only in the order _____, tube anemones
Cnidaria.fact: Ptychocysts are found only in the order Ceriantharia, tube anemones.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: ("cnida" is derived from the _____ word κνίδη, which means "nettle") A tube-like extension of the wall of the cnida that points into the cnida, like the finger of a rubber glove pushed inwards
Cnidaria.fact: ("cnida" is derived from the Greek word κνίδη, which means "nettle") A tube-like extension of the wall of the cnida that points into the cnida, like the finger of a rubber glove pushed inwards.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: At least four hypotheses have been proposed: _____ contraction of fibers round the cnida may increase its internal pressure
Cnidaria.fact: At least four hypotheses have been proposed: Rapid contraction of fibers round the cnida may increase its internal pressure. The thread may be like a coiled spring that extends rapidly when released.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: In the case of _____ (the "sea wasp"), chemical changes in the cnida's contents may cause them to expand rapidly by polymerization
Cnidaria.fact: In the case of Chironex (the "sea wasp"), chemical changes in the cnida's contents may cause them to expand rapidly by polymerization.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: Cnidarians are a very ancient phylum, with fossils having been found in rocks formed about _____ years ago during the Ediacaran period, preceding the Cambrian Explosion
Cnidaria.fact: Cnidarians are a very ancient phylum, with fossils having been found in rocks formed about 580 million years ago during the Ediacaran period, preceding the Cambrian Explosion.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: Other fossils show that corals may have been present shortly before _____ years ago and diversified a few million years later
Cnidaria.fact: Other fossils show that corals may have been present shortly before 490 million years ago and diversified a few million years later.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: Molecular clock analysis of mitochondrial genes suggests an even older age for the crown group of cnidarians, estimated around _____ years ago, almost 200 million years before the Cambrian period, as
Cnidaria.fact: Molecular clock analysis of mitochondrial genes suggests an even older age for the crown group of cnidarians, estimated around 741 million years ago, almost 200 million years before the Cambrian period, as well as before any fossils.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: Cnidocytes can only fire once, and about _____ of a hydra's nematocysts are lost from its tentacles when capturing a brine shrimp
Cnidaria.fact: Cnidocytes can only fire once, and about 25% of a hydra's nematocysts are lost from its tentacles when capturing a brine shrimp.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: However, the agile box jellyfish are unique among _____ because they possess four kinds of true eyes that have retinas, corneas and lenses
Cnidaria.fact: Medusae and complex swimming colonies such as siphonophores and chondrophores sense tilt and acceleration by means of statocysts, chambers lined with hairs which detect the movements of internal mineral grains called statoliths. However, the agile box jellyfish are unique among Medusae because they possess four kinds of true eyes that have retinas, corneas and lenses.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: Although the eyes probably do not form images, _____ can clearly distinguish the direction from which light is coming as well as negotiate around solid-colored objects
Cnidaria.fact: Although the eyes probably do not form images, Cubozoa can clearly distinguish the direction from which light is coming as well as negotiate around solid-colored objects.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: Most obtain the majority of their food from predation but some, including the corals _____ and Leptogorgia, depend almost completely on their endosymbionts and on absorbing dissolved nutrients
Cnidaria.fact: Most obtain the majority of their food from predation but some, including the corals Hetroxenia and Leptogorgia, depend almost completely on their endosymbionts and on absorbing dissolved nutrients.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: For example, in _____ (jellyfish) and Cubozoa (box jellies), a larva swims until it finds a good site, and then becomes a polyp
Cnidaria.fact: For example, in Scyphozoa (jellyfish) and Cubozoa (box jellies), a larva swims until it finds a good site, and then becomes a polyp.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: In addition to both of these methods, _____ can split horizontally just above the base
Cnidaria.fact: In addition to both of these methods, Anthozoa can split horizontally just above the base.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: Hydrozoans have a worldwide range: some, such as Hydra, live in freshwater; _____ appears in the coastal waters of all the oceans; and Liriope can form large shoals near the surface in mid-ocean
Cnidaria.fact: Hydrozoans have a worldwide range: some, such as Hydra, live in freshwater; Obelia appears in the coastal waters of all the oceans; and Liriope can form large shoals near the surface in mid-ocean.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: Among anthozoans, a few scleractinian corals, sea pens and sea fans live in deep, cold waters, and some sea anemones inhabit polar seabeds while others live near hydrothermal vents over _____ (33,000
Cnidaria.fact: Among anthozoans, a few scleractinian corals, sea pens and sea fans live in deep, cold waters, and some sea anemones inhabit polar seabeds while others live near hydrothermal vents over 10 km (33,000 ft) below sea-level.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: Reef-building corals are limited to tropical seas between 30°N and 30°S with a maximum depth of _____ (151 ft), temperatures between 20 and 28 °C (68 and 82 °F), high salinity, and low carbon dioxide
Cnidaria.fact: Reef-building corals are limited to tropical seas between 30°N and 30°S with a maximum depth of 46 m (151 ft), temperatures between 20 and 28 °C (68 and 82 °F), high salinity, and low carbon dioxide levels.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: Stauromedusae, although usually classified as jellyfish, are stalked, sessile animals that live in cool to _____ waters
Cnidaria.fact: Stauromedusae, although usually classified as jellyfish, are stalked, sessile animals that live in cool to Arctic waters.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: Cnidarians range in size from a mere handful of cells for the parasitic myxozoans through Hydra's length of 5–20 mm (1⁄4–3⁄4 in), to the lion's mane jellyfish, which may exceed _____ (6 ft 7 in) in di
Cnidaria.fact: Cnidarians range in size from a mere handful of cells for the parasitic myxozoans through Hydra's length of 5–20 mm (1⁄4–3⁄4 in), to the lion's mane jellyfish, which may exceed 2 m (6 ft 7 in) in diameter and 75 m (246 ft) in length.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: A few mineralized fossils that resemble corals have been found in rocks from the _____ period, and corals diversified in the Early Ordovician
Cnidaria.fact: A few mineralized fossils that resemble corals have been found in rocks from the Cambrian period, and corals diversified in the Early Ordovician.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: These corals, which were wiped out in the Permian–Triassic extinction event about _____ years ago, did not dominate reef construction since sponges and algae also played a major part
Cnidaria.fact: These corals, which were wiped out in the Permian–Triassic extinction event about 252 million years ago, did not dominate reef construction since sponges and algae also played a major part.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: During the Mesozoic era, rudist bivalves were the main reef-builders, but they were wiped out in the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event _____ years ago, and since then the main reef-builders have b
Cnidaria.fact: During the Mesozoic era, rudist bivalves were the main reef-builders, but they were wiped out in the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event 66 million years ago, and since then the main reef-builders have been scleractinian corals.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: Hydroconozoa is an extinct class of cnidarians, established by K.B. Korde in _____ based on Lower Cambrian fossils from Tuva, USSR
Cnidaria.fact: Hydroconozoa is an extinct class of cnidarians, set up by K.B. Korde in 1964 based on Lower Cambrian fossils from Tuva, USSR.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: These conical and cylindrical organisms, including genera like _____ and Tuvaeconus, possessed external skeletons with features resembling both scyphozoans and tetracorals
Cnidaria.fact: These conical and cylindrical organisms, including genera like Hydroconus and Tuvaeconus, possessed external skeletons with features resembling both scyphozoans and tetracorals.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: A study in _____ proposed that Agmatans belong to the cnidarian group rather than constituting their own separate phylum
Cnidaria.fact: A study in 2025 proposed that Agmatans belong to the cnidarian group rather than constituting their own separate phylum.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: In addition, these two groups have been found to likely be each other's closest relatives which, if true, would form the clade "_____"
Cnidaria.fact: In addition, these two groups have been found to likely be each other's closest relatives which, if true, would form the clade "Endocnidozoa".

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: The relationships within the _____ are currently probably the most contentious part of the tree
Cnidaria.fact: The enigmatic Polypodium hydriforme and subphylum Myxozoa have been firmly placed within the Cnidaria and have been shown to be closely related to the Medusozoa. The relationships within the Medusozoa are currently probably the most contentious part of the tree.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: Traditionally, the class _____ also included Staurozoa and Cubozoa, but significant morphological differences eventually lead to the split of the three
Cnidaria.fact: Traditionally, the class Scyphozoa also included Staurozoa and Cubozoa, but significant morphological differences eventually lead to the split of the three. A relationship between Scyphozoa and Cubozoa with Staurozoa as its sister has seen support in nearly all studies, but the position of the remaining class, Hydrozoa, is not understood.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: A relationship between _____ and Cubozoa with Staurozoa as its sister has seen support in nearly all studies, but the position of the remaining class, Hydrozoa, is not understood
Cnidaria.fact: Traditionally, the class Scyphozoa also included Staurozoa and Cubozoa, but significant morphological differences eventually lead to the split of the three. A relationship between Scyphozoa and Cubozoa with Staurozoa as its sister has seen support in nearly all studies, but the position of the remaining class, Hydrozoa, is not understood.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: The group containing them has since been named "_____"
Cnidaria.fact: The group containing them has since been named "Acraspeda". Several studies have found that Acraspeda is paraphyletic, with Hydrozoa being more closely related to Scyphozoa than to the other classes.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: Several studies have found that _____ is paraphyletic, with Hydrozoa being more closely related to Scyphozoa than to the other classes
Cnidaria.fact: The group containing them has since been named "Acraspeda". Several studies have found that Acraspeda is paraphyletic, with Hydrozoa being more closely related to Scyphozoa than to the other classes.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: The relationships between these three and _____ have since and still are debated
Cnidaria.fact: The relationships between these three and Hydrozoa have since and still are debated. A relationship between Scyphozoa and Cubozoa with Staurozoa as its sister has seen support in nearly all studies, but the position of the remaining class, Hydrozoa, is not understood.

Cnidaria.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Cnidaria.question: At the same time, other studies have recovered _____ as being monophyletic
Cnidaria.fact: Several studies have found that Acraspeda is paraphyletic, with Hydrozoa being more closely related to Scyphozoa than to the other classes. At the same time, other studies have recovered Acraspeda as being monophyletic.
